title: Recover shadowed usage credits caused by delayed ACK sync between Hosted/Dedicated/Private paths
creator: Maya Chen
description: Several customers reported negative invoice adjustments and duplicated ledger entries following a multi-region failover combined with a private-deploy KMS rotation. Initial triage showed that asynchronous ACK replay from proxy reconnects caused 'shadowed' credits: tokens consumed in one path were re-attributed when an alternate routing path reconciled late. This ticket scopes investigation, mitigation, and customer-facing remediation across Hosted, Dedicated and Private deployments.
acceptance_criteria: Root cause reproduced in an isolated staging cluster for Hosted/Dedicated/Private mix
A patch merged that prevents double-attribution on delayed ACK replay across proxy rebinds
Backfill reconciliation job created and run to correct affected ledgers with audit trail
Customers with confirmed impact have ledger adjustments applied and outreach completed
New monitoring alerts and a short runbook added to prevent recurrence
steps_taken: 03/10: Pager notified; created initial breakpoint reproducer using captured production traces
03/11: Reproduced delayed-ack condition in staging with proxy reconnect + KMS rotation scenario
03/12: Instrumented attribution path and added idempotency checks in ingest pipeline to capture missing idempotency keys
03/13: Built reconciliation prototype that compares event stream vs ledger and flags candidate shadowed credits
03/14: Drafted rollback/patch PR and coordinated with security for private deployment KMS handling
findings: Root cause: ACKs from the legacy proxy multiplexer were replayed without the canonical attribution header (x-redwood-attr-id) after a KMS rotation changed encryption wrappers, so downstream ledger rehydration treated the replay as a fresh allocation

Edge case: when fallback routing triggered (Hosted fallback to Dedicated) within a 30s window and the proxy reconnect dropped the original idempotency token, the same request was counted twice across two ledgers
Observability: existing metrics aggregated at hour-boundary masked short-lived double-attribution events; no fast alert fired
Customer pattern: affected tenants showed small per-request deltas which cumulatively produced negative invoice adjustments during end-of-month pruning
proposed_fix: Persist canonical attribution (x-redwood-attr-id) at the proxy layer and ensure idempotency keys survive KMS wrapper rotations; add defensive de-duplication at the ledger ingest by checking recent attribution IDs with a short TTL cache. Ship rollout as runtime-1.22 hotfix with an opt-in reconciliation job for past 7 days of activity.
rollout_plan: Stage: Deploy hotfix to staging and run full synthetic scenario that combines KMS rotation + proxy reconnect + fallback routing
Canary: Deploy to one Dedicated cluster and one Private customer region for 24 hours with sampling enabled
Gradual: Expand to remaining Dedicated clusters over 48 hours; then Hosted infra flash rollout
Backfill: Run reconciliation job in read-only mode on affected tenants for validation, then apply corrections in an atomic ledger commit
Post-deploy: Monitor billing metrics and open customer support cases for confirmation
tests: Unit tests for idempotency persistence across KMS wrap/unwrap
Integration test that simulates proxy reconnect and validates attribution ID survives
E2E staging run that asserts no duplicate ledger entries in mixed routing scenarios
Reconciliation job dry-run with seeded shadowed entries and verification of proposed corrections
notes: Link to initial customer escalation: support-ticket #CS-7128 (internal) — customers reported unexplained negative credits on 2026-03-08

Engineering trade-off: short TTL de-dup cache adds memory overhead on ingestion nodes; measured impact ~3% CPU on small nodes, acceptable for P1 fix
